liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Mighty Quinn (Quinn The Eskimo)** (4 reviews, 1 other source): Reviewer says this was the first Quinn the Eskimo and probably the best one; Garcia is on top of every note in Quinn, sounding bright and melodic [3][20][22][23][25]
- **He's Gone** (3 reviews, 1 other source): He's Gone is described as very stretched out; He's Gone is played in a low-key, thoughtful way [3][21][22][23]
- **Crazy Fingers** (3 reviews): The Crazy Fingers into jam into drums stretch is singled out as great; The mid-song solo in Crazy Fingers is called perfect and totally spacey [21][25][26]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (1 review): Sugar Magnolia is described as rocking [26]

## The recordings

- **gd1985-12-30.sbd.miller.77405.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 137 min; rated 4.1/5 by 10 [1]
- **gd1985-12-30.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.106019.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 139 min; rated 4/5 by 5 [2]
- **gd1985-12-30.169534.sbd.marcus.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: soundboard; 20 songs; 139 min [3]
- **gd1985-12-30.schoeps.GEMS.evans-waddell.81314.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 20 songs; 140 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [9]. Said about its sound: Audience recording is less clear than the board but feels more like a live concert; the board sounds like a rehearsal tape [31]
- **gd85-12-30.sbd.georges.1223.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 134 min; rated 4.4/5 by 10 [11]. Said about its sound: Archive version of the soundboard is described as very crisp and well balanced; Reviewer finds the soundboard's sound only so-so compared with other shows downloaded from the same site [21][23]

## Around the show

- Reviewer thinks this show beats the New Year's Eve show the following night [20]
- Reviewer says strong performances were rare in the mid-to-late 1980s compared with the 1970s, but this is one [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1985-12-30.sbd.miller.77405.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Paul Scotton and Joani Walker; transferred by Charlie Connor; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Sony D5/Maxell MX-90) [1]. Also: Commenter argues a DAT copy from a Healy board was unlikely, since Healy didn't use DAT until years later [29]
- **gd1985-12-30.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.106019.flac16**: taped by Joani Walker and Paul Scotton; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Sony D5/Maxell MX-90) [2]
- **gd1985-12-30.169534.sbd.marcus.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Steve Marcus; transferred by Bob Menke, Charlie Miller, Scott Clugston; source: Steve Marcus' Master Soundboard Cassettes > Sony WM-D6C (Maxell MX-90) [3]
- **gd1985-12-30.schoeps.GEMS.evans-waddell.81314.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Jamie Waddell; source: Digital FOB Audience Tape - Taper Unknown. Schoeps Hypercardiods > PCM > DAT [9]
- **gd85-12-30.sbd.georges.1223.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBDmc> DAT> CD> EAC [11]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Oakland Coliseum Arena - December 31, 1985](https://www.dead.net/show/december-31-1985) [33]
- Poster by Brian Baumwoll Grateful Dead: [1985-12-30 Oakland-Alameda County Coliseum, Oakland, CA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1985-12-30-oakland-alameda-county-coliseum-oakland-ca-usa/) [34]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead NYE 1985!](https://www.dead.net/fanphotos/nye-1985) [35]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Oakland Coliseum Arena - December 30, 1985](https://www.dead.net/show/december-30-1985) [36]

claims.text: Reviewer says this was the first Quinn the Eskimo and probably the best one
Reviewer thinks this show beats the New Year's Eve show the following night
Archive version of the soundboard is described as very crisp and well balanced
He's Gone is described as very stretched out
The Crazy Fingers into jam into drums stretch is singled out as great
Garcia is on top of every note in Quinn, sounding bright and melodic
He's Gone is played in a low-key, thoughtful way
Reviewer says strong performances were rare in the mid-to-late 1980s compared with the 1970s, but this is one
Reviewer finds the soundboard's sound only so-so compared with other shows downloaded from the same site
Quinn is named as one of the two highlights of the show
He's Gone is named as one of the two highlights of the show
The mid-song solo in Crazy Fingers is called perfect and totally spacey
The jam after Crazy Fingers keeps going, as if Garcia doesn't want to stop playing
Quinn is called the tightest-sounding version, and reviewer says the band never matched it later
Reviewer has loved this Crazy Fingers since getting the tape in 1985
Sugar Magnolia is described as rocking
Commenter argues a DAT copy from a Healy board was unlikely, since Healy didn't use DAT until years later
Audience recording is less clear than the board but feels more like a live concert; the board sounds like a rehearsal tape
Soundboard cassette master transferred via Sony decks and a Prodif Plus to FLAC by Charlie Miller, from Paul Scotton and Joani Walker cassettes
Soundboard transfer sourced from tapes supplied by Joani Walker and Paul Scotton, with mastering by Miller
Master soundboard cassettes from Steve Marcus, transferred by Bob Menke; a 0:39 patch in Space comes from a Sennheiser ME80 source
Notes mark this as the first performance of The Mighty Quinn (Quinn The Eskimo)
A Smokestack Lightning/Spoonful tease appears within He's Gone
